claims.content: The Customer wants to place a bid on an auction item for sale.
Customer
The Customer is a registered user with a successfully established JTVauctions.com account and a unique Member ID (Handle); guest checkout is not available.
The Customer's account is active and has not been closed or suspended.
The Customer's account has not been flagged by the Consumer Protection negative file.
The Customer has no previous JTVauctions account that was closed by JTVauctions; such a closure would prevent the Customer from placing bids.
The Customer is signed in to the auction site.
The Customer has provided the required minimum information needed to bid.
The Customer has agreed to be bound by the Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer meets the age eligibility requirement for using the Website: they are 18 or over, or are between 13 and 18 and using the Website with permission of a parent or guardian.
The Customer has provided a valid credit card, and any default credit card on file is not expired.
The Customer has no unresolved auction winnings that are more than 7 days old.
The Customer's account is not in Review Status as a result of the auction escalation policy.
The auction item has an available image to display, making it eligible to appear on a product details page, search results, or catalog page.
The auction item is currently open and has not been closed or removed from the listing; closed items are removed within 1 minute (or the configured interval).

The Customer has selected the auction item and is viewing a page where the item and its bid controls are accessible: either the Product Details page dedicated to that item, or a Catalog/List View / listing page that displays the item's card/row with bidding action buttons such as 'QuickBid' and 'SmartBid'; the displayed item includes an image, current price, countdown timer, description, and bidding action buttons as applicable.

The Customer triggers the use case by clicking/tapping one of the bidding action buttons on an item card in the Catalog/List View or on the Product Details Page—such as 'Bid Now', '+$10', '+$25', '+$50', 'QuickBid', 'QuickBid Now', 'Place Bid', 'Place SmartBid', or 'Place Single Bid'—or by clicking the 'SmartBid' button next to an auction item listing; for SmartBid/Single Bid, the Customer first selects/enters a bid amount/value before clicking the corresponding action button.

The Customer initiates the bid by clicking/tapping a bidding action button on an item card in the Catalog/List View or on the Product Details Page—'Bid Now', 'Place Bid', '+$10', '+$25', '+$50', 'QuickBid'/'QuickBid Now', or, after selecting/entering a bid amount, 'Place SmartBid'/'Place Single Bid' (or the 'SmartBid' button next to a listing).

Before allowing the bid to be placed, the system checks the bidder's sign-in status and required minimum information. In the normal case, the Customer is signed in and has the required minimum information, so the system keeps/returns the Customer to the product details page of the item they intended to bid on.

The system determines the bid amount: for QuickBid/QuickBid Now, it automatically enters a single bid higher than the current high bid by adding the displayed bid increment (calculated based on the item's Cost Tier) to the last bid; for SmartBid, it uses the Customer's entered maximum bid amount as an automatic bidding limit; for Single Bid, it uses the Customer's selected specific bid amount.

The system displays a 'Bid Confirm Popup' overlaying the page, showing the bid amount, bid type, and partial credit card number (e.g., 'card ending in 6744'), with a message such as 'You have chosen to bid $[Amount] on this item using a [type] bid, on a credit card ending in [Last4Digits]. Is this correct?' While the popup is active, the rest of the page is grayed out and unclickable.

The confirmation popup presents two options—'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or the equivalent confirmation button) and 'Cancel'—and the Customer confirms the bid by clicking 'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or the equivalent button).
The system places the bid (for QuickBid, this places the QuickBid; for SmartBid/Single Bid, the confirmed bid is submitted) and records the bid to 1/100th of a second.

After a bid placed from the Product Details page, the Customer remains on the product details page; if the bid was initiated as a QuickBid from the Catalog/List View, the system returns the Customer to the catalog page.
If the placed bid was a SmartBid, the system automatically places subsequent bids on the Customer's behalf up to the specified maximum, without requiring manual intervention for each incremental bid.

Diverges from Step 2: If the bidder has not signed in when attempting to place a bid, the system does not proceed with the bid confirmation flow; instead, it takes the bidder directly to the sign-in page. After the Customer successfully signs in (and has provided any required minimum information), the system returns the bidder to the product details page of the item they initially tried to bid on.
Diverges from Step 2: If the Customer clicks the 'QuickBid' button while not signed in, the system prompts them to sign in and then returns them to the catalog page instead of placing the bid.

Diverges from Step 5: Instead of confirming the bid by clicking 'Yes, Place SmartBid' (or the equivalent confirmation button), the Customer clicks 'Cancel' in the Bid Confirmation Popup. The system dismisses the popup and returns the Customer to the ungrayed, interactive Product Details Page without placing or recording any bid. This branch may be used when the Customer notices that the displayed bid amount or the partial credit card number (e.g., 'card ending in 6744') is incorrect or unrecognized.

The system places the bid and immediately records it with a timestamp precise to 1/100th of a second, ensuring accurate chronological ordering in auction history and providing a timestamp for tie-breaking purposes.

After a successful bid is placed from the Product Details page, the Customer remains on the product details page; the page is not grayed out and remains interactive, and no redirect, navigation away, or session termination occurs.
If the successful bid is placed via the QuickBid button from Catalog/List View, the system returns the Customer to the catalog page instead of the product details page.

The Item Bid History section on the Product Details page updates to display the new bid with its timestamp; it shows the most recent bids on top, up to a maximum of 25 bids, including bidder member IDs, bid amounts and times, and an indicator if SmartBids are being used with a link explaining SmartBids.
The Current High Bid for the item is updated dynamically to reflect the new bid amount without requiring a page refresh.

If the placed bid was a SmartBid, the system automatically places subsequent bids on the Customer's behalf up to the specified maximum without requiring manual intervention for each incremental bid; the date/time stamp for computer-generated SmartBids is the time the computer placed the last bid, not the time the Customer placed the original SmartBid.

The system displays the Customer's bid in the 'My Watch List' table with updated data fields: 'Current High Bid' reflects the new amount, 'Total Bids' increments by one (or reflects the updated count), and 'Last Bid Time' updates to the specific time of the transaction.
The 'Action' column for the item in the 'My Watch List' retains the 'Bid' button, indicating that the Customer can place further bids on the same item.

The system updates the 'My Current Bids Page' to include the item in the list of items the Customer is currently bidding on; if the placed bid amount is less than the Current High Bid, the dollar amount in the 'My Current Bid' column appears in bold red text.

The system records the bid in the Customer's 'My Bid History' page, which lists items previously bid on (including both won and not won), sorted by ending time with the most recent on top; the Item # associated with the bid becomes a link to the Product Details (Bidding) page.

The system records the Customer's bid details in the 'Bid History' section of the account history page, capturing the Closed Date/Time, Auction Sequence number, Item Number, Last Bid amount, Max Bid/SmartBid amount, and Winning Bid amount.
If the placed bid is currently the highest, the system updates the bid status to 'Active' in the Bid History view.

If Overtime Bidding is enabled and the bid is placed within the configured duration of the scheduled auction end, the auction timer extends automatically by that configured duration, changing the auction state from 'Ending' to 'Extended'.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger allows the Customer to start the use case by clicking a bidding action button on an item card in Catalog/List View, or by clicking the SmartBid button next to an auction item listing, but Preconditions only require the Customer to be viewing a page dedicated to that item (the Product Details page). No precondition covers the Catalog/List View / listing entry path, so the Trigger has an uncovered implicit prerequisite.

Main Flow step 7 only specifies that after a bid placed from the Product Details page the Customer remains on the Product Details page. However Main Flow step 1 and the Trigger also allow the bid to be initiated from Catalog/List View via QuickBid, and Postconditions require that a QuickBid initiated from Catalog/List View returns the Customer to the catalog page. The current Main Flow does not define that branch, so the catalog-return postcondition is not reachable.

The Trigger explicitly lists 'Place Bid' as one of the bidding action buttons that starts the use case, but Main Flow step 1 does not include 'Place Bid' among the initiating actions; it only lists 'Place SmartBid'/'Place Single Bid'. A bid initiated via the 'Place Bid' button therefore has no corresponding first step.
